intended_object: This is a technical side condition (a "census hypothesis") on a degeneration specification `DegSpec 6 9`, which is a 6-vertex, 9-edge certificate. The condition says that two vertices with the same `rep` value are joined by a chain of zero-length edges in the core graph. I inferred this from the docstring and from how the file uses it as a hypothesis of the ramp and march lemmas.
explanation: `RepGen` is a hypothesis built for one proof. It belongs to the certificate machinery of the genus-four case `GenusFourRow097Closed` and is specialised to a fixed `DegSpec 6 9`. The file uses it only as an assumption of internal lemmas (`vRamp`, `pRamp`, `state_v`, `reaches_core`, `bnExists_one_three`, ...). The docstring describes it as "the census hypothesis every closed-orthant march needs", which the `RowProof.censusSpec` instance satisfies automatically. The literature has no standard object that it is meant to formalise, so it is an auxiliary device of this computer-assisted case analysis, not a mathematical definition.
